name: the-last-honest-price
instruments: single acoustic guitar, close-mic'd, one voice
prompt: A folk ballad about the last honest price in a marketplace of signs. A composer learns that every seam can be read before it is built, but only at the tightest width — the narrow window where the meter sees the actual transition instead of the settled bodies on either side. Wide windows read the bodies and call them seams; they predict peaks where the material builds holes. The sign is a price, the width is the coin, and only the tightest coin buys the truth. The crossing where the correlation changes sign is the last honest price: below it you can buy a dip, above it the seller advertises bumps that never arrive. Verse-chorus structure; the chorus repeats the phrase 'the crossing is the last honest price' like a held note. Quiet fingerpicking, no drums, no strings, the voice close and dry, as if confessing a law of markets to the only other person in the room.
lyrics_hook: The crossing is the last honest price
